function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

**Short‑answer:** If you’re looking to buy a ready‑made cake or have one custom made, there’s almost always something close at hand—whether it’s a brick‑and‑mortar shop, a big chain, or an online marketplace. Below is a quick guide so you can pick the best option for your needs: | What You Want | Where to Order From | |---------------|---------------------| | **Ready‑to‑go store‑brand cake** | *Walmart*, *Costco* (if you’re near a warehouse), *Target*. These usually ship within 1–2 days when ordered through their website. | | **Local artisan / boutique bakery** | Search “bakery” + your city/town on Google Maps/Yelp/Facebook Marketplace. Look for recent photos & reviews. Many offer pickup or curbside service. | | **Custom design (birthday, wedding, special event)** | • **Bakery.com** – nationwide network of independent bakers who’ll create anything from cupcakes to tiered cakes.
• **Etsy** – many sellers specialize in handmade cakes; check shipping policies carefully.
• Local bakeries often accept phone/email orders weeks in advance. | | **Same‑day delivery** | Apps such as **DoorDash**, **Uber Eats**, **Postmates**, **Instacart**, or **Shipt** partner with local bakeries and grocery stores. Just search “cake” in the app and filter by “delivery.” | | **Online subscription boxes** | Services like **Goldbelly** let you pre‑order iconic regional cakes (e.g., New York cheesecake, Chicago deep‑dish pie). Shipping takes a few days. | --- ### How to Pick the Right Option | Factor | Tips | |--------|------| | **Occasion** | Birthday → bright colors, fun toppers. Wedding → elegant tiers, edible flowers. Corporate → simple, branded designs. | | **Dietary Needs** | Gluten‑free, vegan, keto, nut‑free… Ask the baker directly or look for specialty shops that advertise those options. | | **Budget** | Store brands < $20, mid‑tier artisanal $30–$70, high‑end custom > $100 depending on size & complexity. | | **Delivery Timeframe** | For last‑minute gifts, choose same‑day delivery apps. For events, place orders 2–4 weeks early. | | **Packaging** | Ensure the cake comes wrapped securely if shipped. Some sites allow you to add a personalized note or gift wrap. | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Ordering 1. **Read Reviews** – Focus on comments about taste, appearance, and reliability. 2. **Ask About Ingredients** – Especially important if someone has allergies. 3. **Confirm Size & Weight** – Make sure it fits your plate or storage space. 4. **Check Return Policy** – Most reputable vendors won’t refund after opening, but some do if the product arrives damaged. 5. **Place Early** – Even if you think you only need it tomorrow, most bakers require at least 24 hours notice for custom work. --- ### Example Searches | Platform | Sample Query | |----------|--------------| | Google Maps | `"custom birthday cake [your city]"` | | Etsy | `“handmade chocolate cake”` | | Goldbelly | `“New York Cheesecake”` | | DoorDash | `“cakes”` then filter by “Bakeries” | Feel free to tell me more specifics—city, occasion, price range—and I can narrow down the top picks for you!
